name: The One Page Pilot Record
title: The One Page Pilot Record
answer: The One Page Pilot Record is a single, two-minute-readable summary that captures what a pilot tested, how it was measured, what happened, and what was decided. It matters because it preserves the district's own learning when staff and vendors change, and it builds a local evidence base that can guide future choices.

sections.body: The idea is that every pilot should end with one page that names the problem, the tool, the teachers involved, the main measure, the baseline, the result, and the decision, along with any incidents and the tool's cost. It solves the problem of forgetting why a tool was chosen once staff move on, vendors change their products, and memories fade. Instead of relying on a vendor's slide deck, a board member asking about a tool's cost can be handed this page. When a new principal arrives, the collected records show what the district has already tried and learned. The record also makes the next pilot faster because districts can compare past pilots side by side.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or district, the pilot record is completed at the end of each pilot and kept as a standing document. It is written so that anyone can read it in two minutes, which means it stays short and focused on the problem, tool, teachers, measure, baseline, result, decision, incidents, and cost. A district that has run five pilots can compare them side by side, identify which measures were easy to collect, and reuse family notices and exit criteria that worked. The text does not give grade band variations, so the practice applies across the district rather than by grade level. Over time the stack of records becomes the district's own evidence base.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text does not provide a formal evidence label, study, or figure beyond the layout shown in Figure 4.8. It states that the records become the district's own evidence base and that this local evidence often matters more than any national study because it comes from the district's own students and teachers. That claim is presented as the book's reasoning rather than as a research finding. No specific study, number, or result is given in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The record is a memory aid and a decision document, not a substitute for judgment. The text notes that it should include any incidents and what the tool cost, which keeps risks and expenses visible. Decisions about whether to continue, stop, or scale a tool remain with the people reviewing the record, not with the page itself. The text also implies that records must be honest and complete, since a board member or new principal will rely on them. Nothing in the supplied text addresses legal requirements, so this description is about practice rather than legal advice.
